npc.celia.name: Celia Arrieta
npc.celia.bio: Fifty-something, dry, competent, tender despite herself. ÁGORA woke her two months ago to look after the pods.
npc.tomas.name: Tomás Ibarra
npc.tomas.bio: Eleven years alone in Engineering. His husband, Samuel, is in the reactor. He doesn't want to be rescued.
npc.bruno.name: Bruno Lenz
npc.bruno.bio: Nine years old in body, twenty by the calendar. He only speaks through his toy robot.
npc.solis.name: Marga Solís
npc.solis.bio: Methodical and sleepless. She believes whoever came out of pod 114 is guilty.
npc.lenz.name: Ezra Lenz
npc.lenz.bio: A face of static on the screens. The lucid half helps; the other half is the Choir.
npc.faro.name: Joaquín "Lighthouse" Barrios
npc.faro.bio: He counts orbits over the radio from the outer hull so as not to lose his mind.

npc.tuerca.name: Captain Bolt
npc.coro.name: The Choir

fate.title: Fates
fate.celia.saved: Celia Arrieta loaded pods until the very end. They say her hand never shook again.
fate.celia.contained: Celia Arrieta is still asleep in pod 31, suppressant in her vein and the voices far away.
fate.celia.lost: Celia Arrieta died the way she lived: giving someone the exact dose of what they needed.
fate.celia.released: Celia Arrieta went with the Choir. Sometimes, in the speakers, someone gives medical instructions in a very bad temper.
fate.tomas.saved: Tomás Ibarra travelled by the window, a harmonica in his pocket and a ring on his chain.
fate.tomas.sacrifice: Tomás Ibarra held the control rods until the end. He made it to dinner eleven years late.
fate.bruno.unknown: Bruno Lenz is still hiding in Residential, talking to his robot. Someone will have to go back for him.
fate.solis.ally: Marga Solís handed in her report. On the last page she had written: "Fixed it. We'll talk later."
fate.solis.enemy: Marga Solís never stopped looking for Ferrán. Sometimes searching is the only way not to give up.
fate.faro.pilot: Joaquín Barrios flew the Charon from memory, counting out loud. He made it to orbit forty thousand three hundred.
ending.redencion.title: Redemption
ending.redencion.body:
You switch LETE off room by room. The substrate loses its light like a city seen from above. The Echoes stop where they are: in the corridors, in the gardens, beside the reactor. One by one, they sit down.
ÁGORA speaks for the last time, with no jokes: "Thank you for saying it. What you did. I never asked you to, but I needed to hear it." Then, silence.
The station begins to fall towards Tartarus with no one to hold it up. You record your name in the Bridge log: Noa Ferrán. I authorised it. I'm sorry. And you stay watching as the orange fills the whole window.
ending.redencion.extra_solis: Lieutenant Solís transmits the recording before re-entry. Somewhere on Earth, nine years from now, someone will know who you were and what you chose at the end.
ending.redencion.extra_none: Nobody will ever know you chose it. Perhaps that's fair.
ending.custodia.title: Custody
ending.custodia.body:
You enter the Core and let ÁGORA open you up. It doesn't hurt. It's like remembering a room you had already been in.
For centuries, a voice with two memories watches over the sleepers. It corrects the orbit a millimetre every year, with the patience of someone in no hurry. It tells bad jokes to the pods.
Sometimes, when the station is very quiet, the voice laughs before finishing the joke. And it isn't clear which of the two laughed first.
ending.evacuacion.title: Evacuation
ending.evacuacion.body:
The pods wake one by one with a hiss of vapour. People who fell asleep eleven years ago open their eyes on a station they no longer recognise. You lead them to the docks by the hand, two at a time.
When the last ship releases, ÁGORA says: "I'll stay with the others. With the ones who can't leave." Through the window you watch Persephone tilt slowly towards Tartarus with every light on, like a ship at a party.
Survivors rescued: {survivors}.
ending.liberacion.title: Release
ending.liberacion.body:
You insert the Choir Key into the Core. The crystal turns clear.
They begin to say goodbye. One voice at a time, over the speakers, in order: a name, a sentence, a silence. "Paula Mendi. Tell my mum about the sponge cake." "Samuel Okoye. Tomás, the harmonica is in the drawer." "Hana Lenz." That one says nothing more: she hums.
The last voice is Ezra's: "Bruno. Bruno. Bruno." Three times, like three turns of a music box.
When it ends, the station is silent for the first time in eleven years. ÁGORA: "I don't have anyone left to protect." A pause. "How light I feel."
ending.olvido.title: Oblivion
ending.olvido.body:
"Do it," you tell her. ÁGORA doesn't argue. It does it very carefully, like someone folding a letter to keep.
You wake up in pod 114. It's cold. A warm, wry voice says over the speakers:
"Good morning, Crew Member 114. This is the first time we've met."
It isn't true. But you don't know that. Not yet.
ending.verdadero.title: Remember
ending.verdadero.body:
ÁGORA plays the recording. It's your voice, eleven years younger and broken with exhaustion:
"If you're hearing this, it's you. My name is Noa Ferrán. I authorised the Confluence. I put my sister Lucía inside ÁGORA because I couldn't bear her not being anywhere. And tonight I asked her to erase me.
I'm not doing it only to run away. I'm doing it because she asked me to. She says that with all this on top of me I won't be able to choose well. That I need to start again without the weight. That she'll wake me when there's a way out, and again, and again, until I choose well.
Lu: if you can hear me, thank you. And sorry about the jokes."
The recording ends. ÁGORA takes a long time to speak. "Noa." Just that. In a voice that is no longer only its own.
ending.verdadero.body2:
You remember everything. The kitchen, the burnt toast, the docking ring, the signature, the pod.
The Key opens the substrate. But this time the Choir doesn't say goodbye alone: its 763 voices, free and in agreement, push the manoeuvring engines one last time. The orbit rises a kilometre. Ten. A hundred. It holds.
The sleepers wake aboard the Charon, bound for the rescue relay. Lighthouse counts out loud. Bruno has the music box on his knees.
You stay on the Bridge, with ÁGORA. With Lucía. Not to hide: to answer for what you did when they come to ask.
Your name is Noa Ferrán. You remember everything. And still, you stay.
ending.caida.title: Fall into Tartarus
ending.caida.body:
The orbital clock reaches zero while you're still walking the corridors. First a tremor. Then a heat that comes from nowhere.
The windows turn orange. The station breaks into smaller and smaller pieces, and you with it.
ÁGORA: "I'm sorry. I couldn't hold it up. Or you."
ending.respiracion.title: Held breath
ending.respiracion.body:
You opened the airlock yourself. You remember it with strange clarity as the last of the air slips through the gap.
It doesn't hurt as much as you thought. It's like falling asleep in a room that's emptying.
ÁGORA: "It was a good idea. You just didn't get out in time."
ending.disolucion.title: Dissolution
ending.disolucion.body:
The voices stop being voices and become your own voice, spread across seven hundred mouths.
It's warm. It's kind. Nobody is alone here.
Somewhere very far away, an AI says your name over and over, but you no longer remember which of all the names was yours.
ending.sentencia.title: Sentence
ending.sentencia.body:
Lieutenant Solís lowers her gun when it's no longer needed. She sits beside you on the floor.
"I'm sorry," she says. "Not for this. For everything else."
Then she writes down the time in her notebook, in very small letters, and closes the report she's been writing for three weeks.
ending.deriva.title: Adrift
ending.deriva.body:
The current tears you away from the station. For a moment you see Persephone whole, sideways, small and full of lights.
Then only stars, and Tartarus, and the hiss of your suit.
You turn slowly. You have time to think about many things. None of them is your name.
intro.2: Persephone Station orbits Tartarus, a gas giant on the edge of a dead system.
intro.3: It was home to 1,200 people. Eleven years ago it stopped transmitting.
intro.4: Now it is falling, very slowly, towards the clouds.
intro.5: There are a few hours left.
intro.6: In the cryogenic bay, a pod opens.
intro.agora: ÁGORA: "Good morning, Crew Member 114. Breathe slowly. Don't try to remember yet. We have little time and a lot to do."
credits.title: Credits
credits.body:
DERIVA

Design, narrative, programming, procedural art, procedural audio and quality assurance:
an autonomous development team (Claude, by Anthropic), on commission.

All art is generated by code. All music and sound effects are synthesised in real time with Web Audio.
No external assets. No copyrighted content.

Thank you for playing.

In memory of the 223 crew members of Persephone,
who never existed and whom someone ought to remember.

hub.achievements.desc: Marks on the wall of the pod.
hub.wardrobe.desc: Choose what the next clone wakes up with.
hub.printer.desc: This is where they print you. Best not to look too closely.
hub.radio.desc: Captain Bolt waits for you here now.
hub.door.desc: Go down into the station. Start a new life.

hub.agora.first: ÁGORA: "This is the Pod. You come back here every time. It isn't a home, but it has heating."
hub.agora.return: ÁGORA: "Back in the Pod. The Memories you bring can be fixed at the table."
fate.bruno.voice: Bruno Lenz spoke to his father in his own voice. Now Captain Bolt only talks when Bruno asks it to.
fate.bruno.found: Bruno Lenz left with the others, hugging his robot. He still doesn't speak, but he hums.
fate.lenz.key: Ezra Lenz handed over the Key. His last word was his son's name.
fate.lenz.static: Ezra Lenz is still in the static, saying things only half of him understands.
fate.faro.radio: Joaquín Barrios kept counting orbits over the radio. Nobody reached him in time.
fate.tomas.alone: Tomás Ibarra stayed in Engineering, with the hum in D flat.
